entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11591"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 30</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ezek.30.1-Ezek.30.26">Eze 30:1-26</reference>. Continuation of the Prophecies against Egypt.</title> <div sID="gen21004" type="x-p"/> Two distinct messages: (1) At <reference osisRef="Ezek.30.1-Ezek.30.19">Eze 30:1-19</reference>, a repetition of <reference osisRef="Ezek.29.1-Ezek.29.16">Eze 29:1-16</reference>, with fuller details of lifelike distinctness. The date is probably not long after that mentioned in <reference osisRef="Ezek.29.17">Eze 29:17</reference>, on the eve of Nebuchadnezzar's march against Egypt after subjugating Tyre. (2) A vision relating directly to Pharaoh and the overthrow of his kingdom; communicated at an earlier date, the seventh of the first month of the eleventh year. Not a year after the date in <reference osisRef="Ezek.29.1">Eze 29:1</reference>, and three months before the taking of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar.<div eID="gen21004" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21005" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11591"/><hi type="bold">2. Woe worth the day!--</hi>that is, Alas for the day! <div eID="gen21005" type="x-p"/>

(2) A vision relating directly to Pharaoh and the overthrow of his kingdom; communicated at an earlier date, the seventh of the first month of the eleventh year. Not a year after the date in Eze 29:1 , and three months before the taking of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar. 2. Woe worth the day!-- that is, Alas for the day!

So in <reference osisRef="Ezek.30.18">Eze 30:18</reference>, "daughters shall go into captivity" [Maurer]. <div eID="gen21024" type="x-p"/>

Tehaphnehes--</hi>called from the queen of Egypt mentioned in <reference osisRef="1Kgs.11.19">1Ki 11:19</reference>.
